entities.name: Abadiu of Antinoe
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abadiu of Antinoe (4th century CE) was a bishop of Antinoe (Antinoöpolis) in Egypt, a city founded by the Roman Emperor Hadrian in honour of his favourite Antinous on the east bank of the Nile in Middle Egypt. He is commemorated as a saint in the Coptic Orthodox Church, which preserves the traditions of Egypt's ancient Christian communities.

Antinoe was a significant urban centre in Roman and Byzantine Egypt, notable both as an administrative hub and as a site of early Christian community. Bishops of Antinoe participated in the councils and controversies of the early Church, and the city's Christian community produced martyrs and confessors during the Roman persecutions. Abadiu's episcopate falls within the period when Egyptian Christianity was consolidating its distinctive monastic and theological character.

His commemoration in the Coptic calendar reflects the Coptic Church's practice of venerating the bishops of Egypt's ancient sees as pillars of the faith, regardless of the historical record's sparseness. The Coptic Orthodox Church, which traces its origins to Saint Mark the Evangelist's mission to Alexandria, has maintained the memory of thousands of early bishops as part of its unbroken apostolic tradition.
